delete.title: Delete document series - {{entry}}
delete.label: Delete
delete.confirm: Deleting a series removes its counter for good. Are you sure you want to delete this document series?

help.intro: A series is the counter behind the reference a person reads on an invoice, an order, a goods receipt or a subscription. It holds only two things worth allocating — a code and the next number — and how those are rendered into INV-000142 is left to whatever displays the document.
help.step_1_body: Invoice, order, GRN and subscription each take exactly one, and a second for the same type is refused. The type is what an allocation resolves on, which is why the field is locked after creation — moving it would hand numbers already issued to a different series.
help.step_2_body: Up to ten characters, and it is the prefix references are built from. It can be changed later, but only documents numbered after the change carry the new one — the old references keep the code they were issued with.
help.step_3_body: Start number is the first number handed out, which is how a series takes over from a legacy numbering rather than restarting at one. On a brand-new series the counter equals it.
help.step_4_title: Let the counter move on its own
help.step_4_body: The next number is never edited here. It advances only when a document takes a number, inside that document's own transaction — a failed save rolls the number back, which is what keeps the sequence gapless. Raising the start number on a series that has already issued documents records an intent and changes nothing about what comes next.
help.step_5_body: Filter by document type, or search the code from three characters — an all-digit term is treated as an id. The list orders by id or code, and there is rarely more than a handful of rows here.
help.note: Deleting a series is permanent and unguarded: there is no deleted state, so nothing can be restored, and nothing stops the removal of a series that has issued numbers. Recreating it starts the counter again from its start number, and the next document collides with references that already exist under that code.
